A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dataset and benchmarking work, renamed from FaceVid-1K to DH-FaceVid-1K. Text, tables, figures, and the later version's appendices are readable and support comparison; v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, text-to-video, image-to-video and unconditional-generation experiments, and a model/data-scale study in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original generation benchmarks and scaling experiments, plus appendix quality analyses, cross-dataset evaluation, qualitative generalization tests, and a user study.

M1.justification: The core collection, cropping, CodeFormer restoration, and PLLaVA annotation workflow remains. v2 extends dataset construction with DWPose facial-keypoint extraction, an additional audio-synchronization filter using retrained SyncNet, and reported age-based filtering; these are component additions within the retained pipeline.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates text-to-video, image-to-video, and unconditional generation; v2 removes unconditional generation. Appendix G and Figures 15–16 add distinct test scenarios involving wild and cartoon-style image inputs, half-body framing, and non-talking actions such as reading.

E2.justification: The single Open-Sora-Plan text-to-video benchmark becomes a five-model comparison using AnimateDiff, Latte, OpenSora, EasyAnimate, and CogVideoX. Image-to-video retains SVD and adds I2VGen-XL, ConsistI2V, EasyAnimate, and CogVideoX. Latte's participation shifts from unconditional generation to text-to-video.

E3.justification: The scaling study changes from Open-Sora-Plan with 1B/3B/6B configurations to CogVideoX with 2B/5B configurations across both conditional tasks. The stated main-text budget changes from 100k to 30k steps, although v2 Appendix E contradictorily specifies 100k. v2 also introduces additional evaluation metrics, a cross-dataset reference mixture, and a 25-participant, 30-video user-study protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond revising the model/data-scale analysis, v2 adds cross-dataset generalization testing, prompt-format and unusual-image case studies, CodeFormer artifact examples, and VBench dataset-quality analyses. These investigate generalization and failure conditions not examined in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added opinion-score means and quality-score distributions are new outcomes rather than a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 substantially replace and expand the results, while unconditional-generation results disappear. For example, the proposed-dataset SVD FVD/FID values change from 168.32/9.35 to 132.92/18.95 under revised data and settings, not a controlled same-setting comparison. New Tables 6–7 report cross-dataset results and human ratings, including overall opinion scores of 4.47 for the proposed dataset versus 4.01 for CelebV-Text.

T1.justification: Neither version presents substantive mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations. The scaling discussion remains empirical.

C1.justification: The resource contribution is materially revised from 213,500 clips and 1,003 hours to a multimodal collection of 270,043 clips and about 1,200 hours with speech and facial keypoints. Claimed identity coverage changes from over 150,000 to over 20,000. The abstract and introduction emphasize demographic-bias mitigation and conditional-generation scaling benchmarks while dropping unconditional-generation claims.

C2.justification: v2 reframes backbone comparisons around DiT versus UNet quality/resource tradeoffs and revises scaling recommendations for CogVideoX. Its appendices newly discuss CodeFormer artifacts, demographic and action limitations, generalization despite imbalanced attributes, and dataset-mixing recommendations, substantially expanding applicability and failure-condition discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds filtering thresholds, annotation-review procedures and attribute lists, hardware information, model versions, learning rates, checkpoint handling, and detailed test construction. It also provides a project-page link and application-based academic-use conditions. Reproducibility remains weakened by conflicting 30k/100k training budgets and 5B table versus 6B discussion descriptions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cited literature and comparisons with prior resources, including VoxCeleb2 and Casual Conversations datasets. Newer generation backbones and portrait-animation work broaden the positioning, while the Hallo2/Hallo3 comparison explicitly supports the revised architecture/resource discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, dataset statistics are consolidated, and the motivation and experimental narrative are reorganized into numbered sections. New audio-filtering and data-safety sections and Appendices A–L substantially change the document structure beyond the dataset rename.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the overview to display audio and annotations, replaces compact benchmark tables with multi-model tables, and rebuilds the qualitative comparison grids. It adds resolution/duration plots, failure examples, annotation displays, quality distributions, and extensive appendix results. Several original figures are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The broader backbone comparisons, cross-dataset evaluation, and user study provide better support for dataset utility than v1's narrow validation, while the appendix improves construction details and limitation reporting. These gains are partially offset by unresolved inconsistencies: 30k versus 100k training steps, 5B results discussed as 6B, and age filtering that conflicts with reported minors. The added evidence is useful, but these problems limit reproducibility and prevent a stronger overall improvement judgment.
